patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Airtable and Microsoft Project share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Frame: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Airtable and Microsoft Project share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.. Choose Airtable only if your buying job matches “Flexible database / app platform with interfaces and light project apps — Team from ~$20/u” rather than Microsoft Project's shape. Choose Microsoft Project only if your buying job matches “Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan ” rather than Airtable's shape. Workflow advantage: Airtable leans shared coverage; Microsoft Project leans resource-planning, timeline-reporting. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Airtable and Microsoft Project share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Airtable is Flexible database / app platform with interfaces and light project apps — Team from ~$20/user/mo annual.; Microsoft Project is Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan 1 from ~$10/user/mo..
- Company-size focus: Airtable (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Microsoft Project (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Airtable-leaning — vs Microsoft Project-leaning resource-planning, timeline-reporting.
- Researched limits: Airtable — Higher seat floors than Notion/ClickUp; Microsoft Project — SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans.

Limitations — Airtable: Higher seat floors than Notion/ClickUp; Builder complexity; Microsoft Project: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans; Best value assumes Microsoft 365 standardisation.

Poor-fit cases: Airtable is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Higher seat floors than Notion/ClickUp · Microsoft Project is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans · Avoid Airtable if you actually need Microsoft Project's motion (Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Pla)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
